policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Purely orthographic qere/ketiv: הנערה (plene) vs consonantal הנער, both read as the feminine noun. ASV 'the father of the damsel' renders the same word either way and carries no note mapped here, so nothing in the English distinguishes the spellings; the qere base fallback carries the projection.

Same orthographic qere/ketiv pair (הנערה / הנער). ASV 'the tokens of the damsel's virginity' translates the identical feminine noun under either spelling and has no mapped textual note, so the English cannot select; base qere retained.

Orthographic qere/ketiv only. ASV 'the damsel's father' reflects the feminine noun that both the plene qere and the defective ketiv are read as; no mapped note, so underdetermined with the qere base fallback.
Spelling variant לנערה / לנער with identical reading and sense. ASV 'found in the damsel' is compatible with both and no ASV note is mapped to this unit; base qere carries the projection.

Qere הנערה against defective ketiv הנער, an orthographic difference the reading tradition resolves to the same feminine noun. ASV 'shall bring out the damsel' does not distinguish them and carries no mapped textual note; underdetermined.
Plene נערה versus defective נער, read alike. ASV 'a damsel that is a virgin betrothed' renders the same noun under either spelling and no note is mapped here; base qere retained.

Orthographic qere/ketiv (הנערה / הנער) with no difference in the word read. ASV 'the damsel, because she cried not' translates it identically either way and has no mapped textual note; underdetermined, qere fallback.

Spelling-only variant. ASV 'find the damsel that is betrothed' is the same rendering of the same feminine noun under plene qere or defective ketiv, and no ASV note is mapped to this unit; base qere carries it.

ולנערה / ולנער differ only in orthography and are read identically. ASV 'but unto the damsel thou shalt do nothing' cannot distinguish them and carries no mapped note; underdetermined with the qere base.
Second orthographic qere/ketiv in the verse (לנערה / לנער). ASV 'there is in the damsel no sin worthy of death' renders the same word either way and no note is mapped here; base qere retained.

Qere הנערה against ketiv הנער, a purely written difference. ASV 'the betrothed damsel cried' is compatible with both spellings and has no mapped textual note; underdetermined, qere fallback carries the projection.

Plene נערה versus defective נער, the same feminine noun in the reading tradition. ASV 'find a damsel that is a virgin' does not select between the spellings and no ASV note is mapped to this unit; base qere retained.

Orthographic qere/ketiv (הנערה / הנער) with identical pronunciation and sense. ASV 'unto the damsel's father' translates it the same under either witness and carries no mapped textual note; underdetermined with the qere base fallback.
